Title: Doctors fear haze's long-term effects [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: General practitioners (GPs) are seeing more patients with respiratory complaints, but private hospitals say they are coping with the haze for now.
With the haze expected to linger for two more weeks, doctors are concerned about the effects of prolonged exposure to polluted air, particularly among vulnerable individuals.
Symptoms include coughing, throat irritation, blocked or runny nose, eye irritation, wheezing and asthma exacerbations.
Federation of Private Medical Practitioners' Associations president Dr G. Shanmuganathan said GPs were seeing more patients with symptoms associated with poor air quality.
"If unhealthy air quality persists for another month, GP clinics should anticipate increasing consultations for cough, throat and eye irritation, wheezing, asthma exacerbations and worsening of existing conditions.
"The concern is not simply one day of exposure. It is repeated exposure over several weeks, particularly among vulnerable individuals," he told the
New Straits Times
.
Dr Shanmuganathan said, however, it was important to distinguish these symptoms from upper respiratory tract infections (URTI).
He said the haze did not cause viral URTI, but symptoms could overlap and pollution could aggravate existing respiratory illnesses.
[[nid:1545891]]
"From the primary-care perspective, if this episode is expected to persist until this month, it would also be useful for the Health Ministry to monitor respiratory attendances in both public and private primary care.
"This would give us an objective picture of the health burden of prolonged haze exposure, rather than having to rely on anecdotal reports from individual clinics."
Meanwhile, Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia president Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh said private hospitals were not seeing any significant increase in admissions linked to the haze.
He said private hospitals were managing respiratory and haze-related cases well and had the capacity to respond should patient numbers increase.
He said there was no pressure on bed occupancy or respiratory wards at present.
[[nid:1545890]]
Dr Kuljit said this was supported by close collaboration between private hospitals, public hospitals and the Health Ministry, allowing for appropriate referrals and coordinated care when required.
"We typically see fluctuations in influenza cases several times throughout the year, and this trend is observed across both private and public hospitals.
"While haze does not directly cause influenza, exposure to poor air quality can aggravate existing respiratory conditions and symptoms, including those associated with influenza and bronchitis."
Dr Kuljit said the association continued to work closely with the ministry to ensure patients received appropriate care and that the healthcare system remained prepared should respiratory and haze-related cases increase further.

Title: US judge denies Lindsay Clancy's acquittal bid over deaths of three children
Article:
NEW YORK: A judge on Thursday denied an acquittal request by an American mother accused of murdering her three children, a court filing showed, weeks after a jury failed to reach a verdict in the high-profile case.
During the trial, 36-year-old Lindsay Clancy did not deny strangling Cora, age five, Dawson, three, and Callan, eight months. But she claimed she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and sought to be excused from criminal responsibility.
Judge William Sullivan, of the Plymouth court near Boston, ruled there was sufficient evidence to convince a juror of Clancy's guilt.
The judge has yet to decide whether she will face a retrial.
In September a jury of nine women and three men was unable to reach a unanimous decision, as required in criminal proceedings in the United States, leading to a mistrial.
Kevin Reddington, who is defending Clancy, had asked the judge to enter a not-guilty verdict, essentially dismissing the case after a weeks-long, televised trial that captivated Americans.
"Where is the evidence she did this?" said Reddington previously. He also cast doubt on Clancy's own admissions that she killed her children, in what would be a major shift from her mental health defense.
Prosecutor Jennifer Sprague disputed the claim of insufficient evidence as a "laughable argument."
Eleven jurors were in favour of finding Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity, but they were opposed by a single holdout who has spoken publicly about being sure of her guilt.
Deliberations lasted seven days.
The prosecution opposed the disclosures, saying they would have a "chilling effect" on the lone juror.
Clancy's trial, which featured more than 80 witnesses and days of distressing testimony, sparked debate in the United States over maternal mental health.
President Donald Trump has called the case a "horrible tragedy" and said he assumed there would be another trial.
Clancy, who is being held at a psychiatric institution, pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity and said she heard a voice ordering her to kill her children.
Her lawyers said this was caused by postpartum psychosis, a condition that medical experts say affects about one to two women in every 1,000 births.
Prosecutors rejected that argument, saying Clancy had carefully planned the murders and was able to understand the consequences of her actions.
After the killings at the family home in Duxbury, Massachusetts in January 2023, Clancy cut her neck and wrists and jumped from a second-story window in an apparent suicide attempt that has left her paralysed from the waist down and confined to a wheelchair.--AFP

Title: Pentagon signs US$24.4bil deal to accelerate missile output
Article:
WASHINGTON: The Pentagon on Thursday announced the award of a US$24.4 billion contract for Raytheon to accelerate production of SM-6 missiles as Washington works to replace the large amount of munitions expended during the Iran war.
The missiles are "critical anti-air and anti-surface warfare munition. This five-year agreement, with two additional option years, will drive faster production," the Pentagon said in a statement.
The deal "provides the defence industry with the long-term predictability needed to expand workforce capacity and secure critical supply chains," the statement added.
President Donald Trump has so far brushed aside questions about the major toll taken on US munition supplies by the war against Iran, which the United States and Israel launched on Feb 28.
But the Defence Department's inspector general said last month that "the munitions expenditure on Operation Epic Fury has resulted in strategic inventory shortfalls and revealed industrial base bottlenecks for munitions resupply," using the official name for the operation against Iran.
And a Sept 15 report by the Congressional Budget Office cited the hit to missile defence supplies that "will leave the United States with a reduced inventory of interceptors for several years."
Teheran continues to exert control over the strategic Strait of Hormuz more than seven months after the initial US and Israeli attacks on the Islamic Republic, while Washington is blockading Iran's ports.
Trump has told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran by late November, the Wall Street Journal reported, which would set the stage for further Iranian strikes and more expenditures of American munitions.--AFP

Title: Teen drowns in Klang lake, Bomba recovers body after two‑hour search
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 2 — A 15-year-old boy drowned while swimming in a lake in Bandar Botanik, Klang yesterday.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 6.21pm.
He said the search operation involved seven personnel from the Andalas station, assisted by the Water Rescue Team (PPDA) from the Shah Alam station.
“The victim is believed to have been swimming alone in the man-made lake and his friends attempted to rescue him.
“The boy’s body was found by the team at a depth of one metre at 8.21pm,” he said in a statement last night. — Bernama

Title: Tampin tragedy: Cable snag topples utility pole, killing motorcyclist, police detain lorry driver
Article:
TAMPIN, Oct 2 — An elderly man was killed after a utility pole fell on him at Felda Jelai here yesterday.
District police chief Supt Amiruddien Sariman said the incident involved the 61-year-old victim, who was riding a motorcycle, and a trailer lorry driven by a 40-year-old man.
He said preliminary investigations found that the victim was travelling from Felda Jelai 3 towards the Felda Jelai Health Clinic, while the lorry was believed to have been exiting a junction from Felda Jelai 4.
“As the lorry was leaving the junction, it is believed to have become caught on a utility cable, causing a pole on the opposite side of the road to topple onto the motorcyclist,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said the victim sustained serious head injuries and died while receiving treatment at the Felda Jelai Health Clinic.
The trailer lorry driver was detained to assist in the investigation, and the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, he added. — Bernama

Title: Bukit Aman confirms arrests: Eight police personnel held over ketum water activities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Eight police personnel were among nine individuals arrested on suspicion of being involved in ketum water-related activities during a raid in Taman Keramat here on Sept 29.
Bukit Aman Integrity and Standards Compliance Department (JIPS) director Datuk Aida Abdul Hamid confirmed the arrests.
She said her department was closely monitoring the case and that a transparent investigation was being carried out by the Ampang Jaya District Police Headquarters (IPD).
“Yes, Bukit Aman JIPS confirms the arrest of eight police personnel along with a civilian in an operation in Taman Keramat,” she said when contacted.
According to sources, the raid was conducted at 8.45pm at Jalan AU1, Taman Keramat here by the Bukit Aman JIPS Intelligence and Operations Branch and the Ampang Jaya District Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division.
“The eight arrested personnel include seven attached to various branches under the Sentul District Police Headquarters (IPD), while another is attached to the Brickfields IPD. A civilian was also arrested,” the source said.
The source added that all suspects are being held at the Hulu Kelang Police Station lock-up and the case is being investigated under Section 30(3) of the Poisons Act 1952. — Bernama

Title: ‘Every corner reminds him of her’: Mukhriz appeals for privacy for Dr Mahathir
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir has appealed to the public and the media to give his father, Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, the necessary time and privacy to grieve following the passing of his beloved wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali.
Mukhriz explained that the loss of his mother continues to weigh heavily on the former prime minister, noting that coming to terms with such a profound separation will require patience and care,
Awani
reported.
“Tun Mahathir, as we can see, has not even gone through a week since the passing of his beloved wife, who had been with him for 70 years. Naturally, it will take time for him to truly come to terms with the fact that my late mother is no longer with us.
“I believe that what is happening now is, to some extent, a manifestation of his emotional and physical condition,” he said.
Mukhriz was speaking to reporters after attending a tahlil and Yasin recitation ceremony held in memory of the late Dr Siti Hasmah at the Saidina Umar Al-Khattab Mosque in Bukit Damansara last night.
He said that being inside the family home has been emotionally difficult for the 101-year-old Dr Mahathir, as nearly every room brings back poignant memories of his late wife.
For that reason, Mukhriz said that it is preferable for Dr Mahathir to remain temporarily at the National Heart Institute (IJN) until his physical and emotional strength improves.
“I think that if he stays at home, everything he sees will remind him of my late mother. So perhaps it would be better for him to remain at IJN until he has fully recovered.
“Today, he also went to visit her grave, and that is a positive development,” he said last night.
Mukhriz urged everyone to empathise with what his father is experiencing and to refrain from placing undue pressure on him during this delicate period of mourning.
“I sincerely appeal to everyone, if possible, not to pressure him too much to find out about his emotional state and so on.
“Imagine if we ourselves were in the same situation. Of course, we too would feel an immense sense of loss. So please give him some space and time to recover on his own,” he said.
Dr Hasmah died at the age of 100 at IJN on September 28, drawing to a close a revered 70-year union that stood as one of the most enduring partnerships in the nation’s history.

Title: Police say plan ahead: Five checkpoints, contra‑flow lanes and diversions as Sepang braces for F1 crowds
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 2 — All vehicles heading to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) for the 2026 Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix will undergo screening at five main locations to ensure smooth traffic flow throughout the event.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the locations are the route from the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) toll plaza towards Jalan Pekeliling; from KLIA1 towards Jalan Pekeliling; before the Masjid Roundabout towards SIC; from Kota Warisan towards Labohan Dagang and Jalan KLIA1; and the junction of Jalan Kuarters KLIA towards SIC at the Enstek traffic lights.
“Vehicles heading to SIC will be screened for tickets, vehicle passes and access stickers before visitors are allowed to enter the circuit,” he told a press conference at the Selangor Police Contingent Headquarters here yesterday.
Shazeli said 365 officers and personnel from the Selangor Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT) would be deployed for traffic control, congestion prevention patrols, law enforcement and VIP escort duties throughout the event.
The traffic operation will run from 9 am to 6 pm daily from today (Oct 2), with the main focus on the race this Sunday (Oct 4).
He said the parking facilities could accommodate 9,000 vehicles across 17 lots, as well as up to 100 buses at one time.
Authorities have also coordinated public transport services to reduce reliance on private vehicles.
“Some 200 e-hailing passes have been issued to Grab, while 100 passes have been allocated to Prestige Lane to pick up and drop off passengers at the Long Term Car Park (LTCP) and selected hotels.
“Mobility services have also been strengthened with 95 MyRapid shuttle buses operating from four pickup locations, along with 50 shuttle buses operated in partnership with Grab at two designated locations,” he said.
Shazeli advised visitors without parking tickets to leave their vehicles near the designated shuttle bus and e-hailing service locations to help ease traffic flow.
He said strict action, including summonses and vehicle towing, would be taken against those who flout the rules, particularly motorists who park on road shoulders in restricted areas.
A tidal flow or contra-flow system will also be implemented along about 13 kilometres of the route between the Masjid Roundabout and SIC.
Road users are advised to follow JSPT personnel’s instructions and comply with temporary signs, cones and lane controls throughout the operation.
“If congestion occurs outside the circuit, motorists travelling from north to south can use alternative routes via the ELITE Expressway, Saujana Putra exit, South Klang Valley Expressway (SKVE) and the KL-Seremban Toll Plaza. Another alternative is the ELITE Expressway, Putrajaya exit, MEX Expressway and the KL-Seremban Toll Plaza,” he said.
Meanwhile, the Road Transport Department (JPJ) and Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) will control and divert heavy vehicles, including lorries, at eight checkpoints: Masjid Roundabout; the junction in front of the F1 Main Entrance; Jalan KLIA S8/Jalan Pekeliling; Jalan B48-Jalan 1266; Persiaran Teknologi 1-Persiaran Milenia 2; Persiaran Teknologi 2-Persiaran Seri Emas Utama; Jalan Merpati-Jalan Besar Salak; and Jalan Besar Salak-Jalan Kuarters KLIA.
Information on routes to SIC and KLIA during the F1 event will also be displayed on digital billboards at the KLIA Toll Plaza. The public are advised to follow instructions from traffic personnel, travel early and plan their journeys carefully.
Passengers using KLIA are also urged to leave earlier to avoid congestion and arrive at the airport on time. — Bernama

Title: Anwar tells Bahrain crown prince Malaysia is revved up to host Formula 1 Grand Prix
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday shared updates on the preparations for the 2026 Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia with Bahrain’s Crown Prince and Prime Minister, Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa.
Anwar said the updates were shared during a phone call on the sidelines of his visit to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) yesterday.
“I also expressed my appreciation for the close cooperation between Malaysia and Bahrain in making this event a success, with all preparations now in full swing to welcome fans and visitors from all over the world.
“I look forward to meeting the Crown Prince in Malaysia in a few days, God willing, while continuing to strengthen the friendship between the two countries,” he said in a Facebook post.
Yesterday, the Prime Minister participated in a Pit Lane Walk in conjunction with the race, which will be held at SIC from tomorrow until Sunday.
Also present were Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif and Bahrain International Circuit (BIC) chief executive Sheikh Salman Isa Al Khalifa.
SIC was chosen to host the 2026 Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix, making the iconic circuit a temporary venue for the prestigious race.
In July, Formula 1 confirmed Malaysia as the host of the race from Oct 2 to 4 following an agreement between F1, the Federation Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA) and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The agreement allowed the Bahrain GP to remain on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race, initially scheduled for earlier this season, was cancelled due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Malaysia previously hosted the Malaysian Grand Prix at Sepang from 1999 to 2017 before it was dropped from the F1 calendar. — Bernama

Title: Clear skies for F1, KL Marathon as air quality improves nationwide; Seri Manjung sole hotspot
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Malaysia is heading into a bumper weekend of major international and national sporting events with clear skies across almost the entire country, as only a single monitoring station recorded unhealthy air quality this morning.
Data from the Department of Environment (DoE) showed Seri Manjung in Perak as the nation's sole location in the unhealthy bracket as of 9am today, registering an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 108.
Every other monitoring station across Malaysia recorded moderate or good air quality with readings of 100 or below, providing timely relief for organisers, athletes, and tens of thousands of spectators ahead of a packed sports calendar.
The cleared conditions mean flagship events, including the Formula One race at the Sepang International Circuit, Le Tour de Langkawi, and the Standard Chartered Kuala Lumpur Marathon, are set to proceed as scheduled.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said earlier this week that the government expects all three major sporting fixtures to run without disruption, noting that the Youth and Sports Ministry is assessing atmospheric conditions daily to safeguard participant welfare.

Title: Akmal Nasrullah highlights upbeat Malaysia–Singapore talks as ministerial committee meets Nov 2 on economic zone plan
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — The first meeting of the Johor-Singapore Cooperation Ministerial Committee (JSCMC) will be held in Singapore on Nov 2.
This comes ahead of the official launch of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) Master Plan at the 13th Malaysia-Singapore Leaders’ Retreat on Dec 4 and 5.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the matter was discussed during a meeting with Singapore Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry Gan Kim Yong at his office here yesterday.
“Our discussion was held in a very positive atmosphere, focusing on efforts to further strengthen Malaysia-Singapore economic cooperation. The key topics were the smooth implementation of the JS-SEZ and the cross-border carbon capture and storage (CCS) initiative,” he said in a post on his official Facebook page.
Akmal Nasrullah said the JS-SEZ has significant potential, with more than S$5.5 billion (RM17.97 billion) in investment commitments from Singapore-based companies recorded as of October 2025. “Now, our focus is on the next phase of implementation. As the ministry responsible for the JS-SEZ initiative, our aim is to ensure its benefits are felt by the people of Johor and Malaysians as a whole,” he added.
On CCS, he said both countries aim to conclude a bilateral agreement in the fourth quarter of this year, marking a strategic step towards developing a regional green value chain. “The close cooperation we have built is not merely about investment figures on paper. Ultimately, the goal is to translate this relationship into quality job opportunities, skills development and sustainable economic growth for the benefit of the people,” he added.
The minister also expressed his appreciation to Gan and the Singapore delegation for the productive discussions.
Gan is on a one-day working visit to Malaysia to strengthen economic ties and supply chain resilience between the two countries. During the visit, he met Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and attended a business luncheon with the Malaysia-Singapore Business Council in Kuala Lumpur.
He also co-chaired the Third Annual Ministerial Dialogue (AMD) between Miti and Singapore’s Ministry of Trade and Industry, besides meeting Akmal Nasrullah in Putrajaya. Gan and his delegation departed for Singapore at 6.35pm. — Bernama

Title: UM to roll out hostel project housing 40,000 students, meeting B40 families’ needs, says Zambry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Universiti Malaya (UM) will provide accommodation for more than 40,000 students through the Student Residential Hostel Project, which is expected to be launched by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Oct 15.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir said the project was among the models being developed by the government to accelerate the provision of student accommodation at public universities, amid growing demand for housing.
“At UM, as I understand it, the residential hostel will eventually meet the needs of more than 40,000 students. It will be built in stages, but the immediate basic needs must also be addressed,” he said after launching the ILMUcode platform by YTL AI Labs here yesterday.
Zambry said priority for the accommodation would be given to students from low-income families, particularly those from the B40 group, including those who come from faraway places and cannot afford to secure accommodation on their own.
He stressed that the project was not intended solely to generate income but to help address students’ accommodation needs, particularly those from low-income families.
Meanwhile, UM vice-chancellor Datuk Seri Prof Dr Noor Azuan Abu Osman said the project would be implemented in two phases, with the first providing accommodation for 10,000 students and the second for 30,000.
In another development, Noor Azuan said ILMUcode was the first artificial intelligence (AI)-based coding platform introduced at UM, enabling developers and students to access advanced coding capabilities at a lower cost.
He said the platform, developed in collaboration with YTL AI Labs, combines an agentic AI coding assistant with the ILMU-GLM-5.3 model to help users understand, write and modify code, as well as resolve software development problems more quickly.
“We are proud that Universiti Malaya is the first university in Malaysia to give our computer science students access to next-generation advanced AI coding through ILMUcode.
“Through ILMUcode, we can equip the next generation of Malaysian technology developers and strengthen the local AI talent pipeline,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Experts call for ‘Ministry of Longevity’ to prepare Malaysia for aged nation status
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Malaysia should coordinate efforts and policies when it comes to longevity and older people, by getting the government, businesses and civil society to work together, National Council of Women's Organisations (NCWO) Malaysia president Prof. Emerita Tan Sri Dr Sharifah Hapsah Syed Hasan has proposed.
Dr Sharifah said there is a need to have a coordinating body, adding that it is up to the federal government on how this body would operate, such as as a council or committee.
She stressed that the coordinating body must be multi-sectoral, which means it should involve not only the government, but also others such as the private sector and non-governmental organisations.
She said the proposed coordinating body would look at policies on creating a society that will not only live longer but also put life to age, and also at all aspects of a longer life.
"It is looking at the economy, looking at the social aspects, looking at the health aspects, looking at the educational aspects. You imagine yourself going towards old age, there's so many things affecting you right, everything that impinges on your life going towards old age. They have to plan together well so that we will move there healthy, curious," she told Malay Mail when met recently at the Employees Provident Fund's (EPF) International Social Wellbeing Conference 2026.
Dr Sharifah said different ministries currently handle different matters relating to older people, such as the National Ageing Blueprint 2025-2045 being under the Ministry of Economy; and the Malaysia Care Strategic Framework and Action Plan (2026–2030) being under the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development.
When speaking about the need for a coordinating body, she noted for example that caregiving and the care industry involves both economic and social aspects.
She said there are also other industries relating to ageing, such as tourism which is a big industry as older people may have different interests when it comes to travel.
During an ISWC 2026 panel session titled "The Long Horizon: From Structural Force to Lived Reality", Dr Sharifah had raised the idea of having a coordinating body or governing body to see through all efforts relating to longevity and older people in Malaysia.
"I think our country lacks that governing body to actually see this through. We have got the blueprint and the strategic plan. But they are belonging to different ministries, you know, so I think somebody must try to coordinate this," she said during the panel session.
Dr Sharifah was responding to a question from moderator Shazana Mokhtar, who asked what could help improve coordination among different government agencies and also external stakeholders.
UK’s National Innovation Centre for Ageing Director Prof Nicola Palmarini speaks during a panel session at the International Social Wellbeing Conference 2026 at Shangri-La Kuala Lumpur on September 29, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Fellow panel speaker and UK’s National Innovation Centre for Ageing (NICA) director, Nicola Palmarini, proposed the idea of setting up a Ministry of Longevity, a feature which he said is missing from current governments globally.
"Probably we need a Ministry of Longevity, because it's a ministry that sees the metrics from very different perspective, it's not simply healthcare, transportation... it's how you connect dots, the data to these elements that helps understand the other factors," the Professor of Ageing, Policy and Planning at Newcastle University said at ISWC 2026.
"Well, I I can say that nobody yet has taken literally this thing so seriously to design what I try to force as a provocation as a Ministry of Longevity," he later said.
He suggested that such a hypothetical ministry could measure the return on different longevity policies, including by measuring all the factors that could influence people living a good and long life, such as education, social factors and pollution.
Earlier in his presentation, he had highlighted Marcella Messina, who is the first-ever official with a longevity portfolio in Italy, with her role being the Councillor for Social Policies, Longevity, Health and Sport in the municipal council of Bergamo in Italy.
Among other things, Palmarini also said there is a need to involve the private sector, as this could create opportunities to accelerate longevity solutions.
J.P. Morgan Asset Management Asia Pacific Chief Market Strategist Tai Hui speaks during a panel session at the International Social Wellbeing Conference 2026 at Shangri-La Kuala Lumpur on September 29, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
JP Morgan Asset Management's Chief Market Strategist (Asia Pacific), Tai Hui, said governments do have a role to play in providing guidance on what is appropriate for the population when it comes to essential services such as healthcare and elderly care.
At the same time, he said the private sector's creativity in providing age-friendly services should not be underestimated.
"For example, in China, we now start to have more package tours designed for the elderly with a less demanding schedule - you don't start at 7am every day, you build in a nap break in the afternoon, you've got softer food being served.
"I remember my dad has a phone which has super-large font size, where it's easier to read, it's simpler to use," he said as a speaker at the same panel session as Sharifah and Palmarini.
"So I think if you give the private sector sufficient room to design and be creative, they can come up with the products that are suitable for the older population as well," he said, indicating that the private sector would design products and services targeted towards older people since they form a large part of the consumer base.
"But there's clearly a public service aspect, which the government has a much bigger role to play, to make sure that it's affordable, is decent quality, and is suitable for the older population," he said.
The ISWC 2026, which was themed "The Long Horizon", is EPF's 13th edition and brought together international and local experts over two days to speak on wide-ranging topics related to longevity.

Title: Anwar vows tighter governance as Madani Government moves to seal leaks and abuse of power
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The government will continue to strengthen public service governance and integrity to combat the leakage of public funds and abuse of power, particularly involving Federal Statutory Bodies, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the matter was among the issues discussed at the Special Cabinet Committee on National Governance (JKKTN) meeting, which he chaired yesterday.
“I stressed that law enforcement must be accompanied by the continuous cultivation of integrity and good governance in the public and private sectors, as well as in society,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
He said the meeting also agreed for a legal study to be conducted to draft the policy, governance direction and the Charities Bill to regulate trust entities and public funding.
The move is crucial to ensure entrusted funds are managed transparently and responsibly, he said, adding that the meeting also agreed to the proposed implementation of the Cultivation of Public Service Values.
At the same time, Anwar said the policy for the Statutory Bodies and Controlled Entities (Financial Governance) Bill will be presented to the Cabinet this year to strengthen discipline and accountability in financial management.
“The meeting also agreed to the seven resolutions presented at the Fifth National Level Governance, Integrity and Anti-Corruption Research Conference on Sept 25,” he said.
Anwar said the Madani Government will continue to strengthen public service integrity and close any avenues for leakages and abuse of power.
“Every ringgit of public money is a trust from the people that must be safeguarded, and every power granted must be used to guarantee their wellbeing,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Electricity bill protection up to 800kWh: What does it mean for a household?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The government has expanded electricity bill protection to domestic users consuming up to 800 kilowatt-hours (kWh) a month, up from the previous 600kWh limit.
The temporary protection, which applies to electricity consumption from September 1 to December 31, exempts eligible households from the Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA), retail charge and eight per cent Sales and Service Tax (SST).
But what does 800kWh actually mean for an ordinary household?
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government expanded electricity bill protection to households using up to 800kWh a month. — Bernama pic
What is 800kWh?
A kilowatt-hour, or kWh, is a unit used to measure how much electricity you use.
A household using 800kWh over a 30-day month averages about 26.7kWh a day.
According to Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB), household electricity consumption depends on factors including the power rating and efficiency of appliances, how many hours they are used, the number of appliances and household usage patterns.
Why was the threshold increased?
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said recent haze and hotter weather had caused some households to use more electricity, pushing their consumption above the previous 600kWh threshold and resulting in higher bills.
The protection was therefore expanded to 800kWh.
This does not mean electricity tariffs have been permanently reduced.
Instead, households consuming 800kWh or less receive temporary exemptions from the AFA, retail charge and SST until the end of December.
Haze and hotter weather have contributed to higher electricity use among some households. — Picture by the Sayuti Zainudin
How much electricity does an appliance use?
If you are not sure how much is your power consumption, TNB has a formula to estimate an appliance’s monthly electricity consumption:
Electricity consumption (kWh) = Power rating (watts) × hours of operation × 30 days ÷ 1,000.
For example, a 100W appliance used for 10 hours a day would consume:
100W × 10 hours × 30 ÷ 1,000 = 30kWh a month.
A 500W appliance used for two hours a day would also consume:
500W × 2 hours × 30 ÷ 1,000 = 30kWh a month.
Almost everything plugged into your home contributes to the total, including lights, fans, televisions, laptops, washing machines, rice cookers, kettles, water heaters and air-conditioners.
Here are some examples of appliances’ monthly electricity use:
What happens if your household uses 800kWh, less or more?
Under the expanded protection, households using 800kWh or less a month are exempted from the Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA), RM10 retail charge and SST.
How much a household saves depends on how much electricity it uses and the AFA rate for that billing period.
The maximum saving is estimated at about RM47 a month, although the amount will differ between households.
This is because the AFA rate can change based on factors such as fuel costs and foreign exchange movements.
Households using more than 800kWh a month will not receive these exemptions.
Consumers should therefore check the kWh figure on their electricity bill, rather than looking only at the total amount payable.
Air-conditioners are among the household appliances that can contribute significantly to monthly electricity consumption. — Unsplash pic
What does 800kWh look like in everyday use?
There is no typical “800kWh household” because electricity use differs depending on the size of the home, number of occupants, appliances and how often they are used.
Think of 800kWh as the total electricity used by everything in your home over one month.
This includes air-conditioners, refrigerators, water heaters, cooking appliances, washing machines, lights, fans, televisions and computers.
For example, an appliance that uses 30kWh a month makes up about 3.75 per cent of the 800kWh threshold.
Several appliances that use relatively small amounts of electricity can therefore add up quickly over a month.
The 800kWh threshold also does not mean households receive 800kWh of free electricity.
It simply determines whether a household qualifies for the temporary exemptions from the specified charges.

Title: MACC remands brothers with ‘Datuk Seri’, ‘Datuk Wira’ titles over alleged RM10m investment abuse
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Two corporate figures, who are brothers, have been remanded for five days over an alleged abuse of position involving an investment of about RM10 million.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) obtained the remand order, effective today until October 5, from Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court this morning.
According to a source, the two men, in their 40s and 50s and carrying the titles Datuk Seri and Datuk Wira, were detained at about 9pm yesterday after giving their statements at the MACC headquarters here.
Initial investigations found that the duo were suspected of acting in collusion in the alleged offence in late 2020.
“They are also believed to have colluded with an officer of an education-based foundation to approve an investment of about RM10 million in an investment company owned by the elder brother,” the source told Bernama.
The MACC also seized 15 luxury cars, 12 high-powered motorcycles, five luxury watches, three bracelets and about RM30,000 in cash.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the matter when contacted and said the case was being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama

Title: Johor government to enhance ‘Smart City’ technology for early extreme weather warnings
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 1 — The Johor government will enhance its ‘Smart City’ technology to enable city residents to receive early flood warnings during extreme heavy rain that poses a risk of flash floods.
State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the early flood warning alerts or notifications would be sent directly to mobile phones via a smart application.
He said it was timely for such initiatives to be implemented so that urgent warning information could be communicated directly to the public, allowing them to take quicker action to safeguard lives and property.
“We need to gather as many mobilephone numbers as possible so that they can immediately start receiving notifications related to extreme weather conditions.
“In Japan, those within a 200 metre to 300 meter radius will receive an early warning notification due to adverse weather conditions.
“Such notifications also warn the public to avoid high risk areas or routes that are likely to be inundated by floodwaters,” Mohd Jafni told reporters at Menara MBJB here today.
Earlier, he chaired an action committee meeting with Johor Bahru City Council (MBJB) officials on the severe flash floods that struck several locations in the city yesterday.
Mohd Jafni explained that two flood warning sirens were operational during yesterday’s flash flood incident, with each sounding three times.
However, he acknowledged that the sirens may not have been loud enough.
“Yesterday, the alarm was triggered three times in Kampung Mohd Amin and near the Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA).
“The issue is that not everyone heard the sirens. So, there is a need to review the system and discuss it with our technical team,” he said.
Yesterday, several parts of Johor Bahru were inundated by flash floods following continuous heavy rain.
Among the severely affected areas were Jalan Ayer Molek, Jalan Yahya, Jalan Pantai, Jalan Wong Ah Fook, and Kampung Pasir in Tampoi.

Title: Johor rolls out additional RM30m after flash floods hit state capital
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 1 — The Johor government will provide an additional allocation of RM30 million next year to fund four urgent measures to address flash flooding in the state capital.
Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the allocation aims to fast-track the implementation of short- and medium-term measures to tackle flash floods.
He said the decision was reached following an action committee meeting earlier today in response to flash flooding that struck several locations in the city yesterday.
“Despite the Johor Bahru City Council (MBJB) spending over RM100 million to address flood measures in the past four years, the weather conditions can be very unpredictable,” he told reporters after an action committee meeting at Menara MBJB here today.
“At present we already have RM48 million allocated for flood mitigation projects for next year, that will be carried out in stages.
“The additional RM30m million allocation for next year will be used to aid existing issues that are not covered under the existing allocation,” he added.
Also present were Johor Bahru Mayor Datuk Mohd Haffiz Ahmad and Perling assemblyman P. Pannir Selvam.
Mohd Jafni said the four key areas of focus include the appointment of specialist consultants by MBJB to conduct a detailed study of the city’s drainage systems and aligning it with the comprehensive district-wide study being carried out by the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID).
“We will also construct underground retention facilities – specifically an On-Site Detention (OSD) system – along the Jalan Sungai Chat area. This involves excavating and building underground concrete tanks to store water, while the surface area can be utilised as a playing field or car park, similar to the project implemented at Kota Iskandar.
“Additionally, we will also increase pumping capacity towards the Johor Straits to manage exceptional rainfall over the next five years.
“In addition, the teams will also deploy mobile pumps to high-risk locations in the city,” he said, adding that the authorities will also upgrade and expand monsoon drains through the Public Works Department (JKR).
Besides the four key areas, Mohd Jafni said various immediate measures would commence by tomorrow.
He said these include deepening the retention pond in Kampung Mohd Amin and lowering existing water levels in ponds such as those in Taman Merdeka and Sungai Chat using a scheduled pumping system prior to heavy rainfall.
“These measures aim to create greater flexible retention capacity to accommodate rainwater runoff.
“At the same time, the integrated coordination involving MBJB, DID, JKR, and the district office would be carried out weekly to continuously monitor the progress of the various flood mitigation projects,” he explained.
Several parts of Johor Bahru were inundated by flash floods yesterday following continuous heavy rain.
Among the severely affected areas were Jalan Ayer Molek, Jalan Yahya, Jalan Pantai, Jalan Wong Ah Fook, and Kampung Pasir in Tampoi.

Title: Bidor petrol station shooting: Police record nine statements, hunt three suspects
Article:
IPOH, Oct 1 — Perak police have recorded statements from nine people, including the victim, in their investigation into the shooting of a businessman at a petrol station in Bidor Sentral last Tuesday.
Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said those whose statements were recorded included three family members who were in the victim’s vehicle, two people in a vehicle near the scene and employees of the petrol station.
He said the victim is now in stable condition after receiving treatment and undergoing surgery at Seri Botani Hospital, while police are investigating from various angles, including identifying the motive, which has yet to be established.
“So far, police have not been able to determine the exact motive for the incident. Once we establish the motive based on the investigation, we will announce it,” he told reporters at the Perak Police Senior Officers’ Mess here today.
Mohd Alwi said police suspected that three individuals were involved in the incident, including a driver, while the registration number of the vehicle used by the suspects was believed to be fake.
He said police had also obtained closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage from the petrol station, which showed the victim being shot from two angles, from the front and the right side.
“We also reviewed CCTV footage at toll plazas and elsewhere, but what we found was that they did not exit the toll.
“However, we are still examining various angles to identify the suspects,” he said.
Police are also investigating the possibility that the victim was being followed, based on the movement of the suspects’ vehicle, which was driven at high speed before stopping in front of the victim’s vehicle and opening fire.
According to Mohd Alwi, the victim is a businessman who owns a restaurant and runs several businesses around Bidor, Sungai Siput and Tapah.
In the incident, the victim, who sustained a single gunshot wound to the left shoulder, was sent to Tapah Hospital for initial treatment. — Bernama

Title: Petronas-Sarawak oil and gas dispute heads to Federal Court for five-day hearing from Jan 25
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — The Federal Court has set five days from January 25 next year to hear petitions filed by Petroliam National Bhd (Petronas) and the Sarawak Government challenging the state and federal laws governing oil and gas matters.
Justice Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang said the petitions would be heard in the order in which they were filed.
However, she left it to the Federal Court panel hearing the petitions to decide whether to first hear the Sarawak Government’s preliminary issue on the validity of the Sarawak (Alteration of Boundaries) Order in Council 1954 (OIC), which concerns the boundaries of Sarawak’s territorial waters.
She said given the fact that the two petitions are not consolidated, the panel hearing the petitions would be in the better position to determine whether the preliminary issue should be heard first.
Justice Rhodzariah made the decision today after the two cases came up before her for summonses for directions.
She also directed parties to file their respective submissions for the petitions as well as for the preliminary issues by January 11 and reply submissions by January 18, and she fixed January 12 for case management.
“The hearing date is fixed from January 25 until January 29, next year,” she said.
Senior state counsel Mohd Adzrul Adzlan, who is representing the Sarawak Government, informed the court that they will be filing an application with regard to their preliminary issue under Rule 23 of the Rules of the Federal Court 1995 within 14 days from today.
Meanwhile, both Petronas and the Sarawak Government will write to the Chief Justice to request an enlarged panel of either a nine-man bench or an 11-man bench to hear the petitions.
Petronas and the Sarawak Government had indicated to the court previously that they wanted their respective petitions to be heard separately. Petronas wants its petition to be heard first, followed by the sequence in which the respective petitions were filed. However, the state government maintains that its petition should be heard first.
The national oil and gas company filed its petition on January 10 this year and obtained leave under Article 4 (4) of the Federal Constitution on March 16 this year, while the Sarawak Government filed its petition on February 23.
In today’s proceeding, Mohd Adzrul argued that the Federal Court panel hearing the petitions should first hear the preliminary issue concerning the OIC before proceeding to hear the petitions. However, Petronas lawyer Datuk Dr Cyrus Das argued that there was no basis to have the legal status of the OIC determined as a preliminary issue and the OIC issue can be taken up in the course of hearing of the petition.
Senior Federal Counsel Ahmad Hanir Hambaly @ Arwi representing the Federal Government, supported the submission by Petronas’s counsel, arguing that its (Petronas’s) petition should be heard first.
Regarding Sarawak Government’s preliminary issue on the validity of the OIC, he said it was not necessary for the issue to be heard by way of a preliminary point of law and the state government can bring up the issue during the main hearing.
On March 16 this year, the Federal Court granted leave to the national oil and gas company to commence proceedings to challenge the legislative competency of the Sarawak State Legislature to enact certain laws and to declare several laws made by the Sarawak State Legislature invalid.
It claimed that the Sarawak State Legislature lacked the competence to enact, modify, amend or revise law with respect to matters under List 1 of the Federal List in the Ninth Schedule of the Federal Constitution.
The Sarawak Government, meanwhile, filed a petition against the Government of Malaysia and Petronas, seeking the Federal Court to determine the constitutional validity and continued applicability of several federal Acts to Sarawak.
The state government, among others, is seeking a declaration that the Petroleum Development Act 1974 (PDA), the Continental Shelf Act 1966 and the Petroleum Mining Act 1966, as applied to Sarawak, were unconstitutional and void ab initio. — Bernama

Title: Don't abuse your power, deputy IGP tells police
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 1 — Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) leaders have been reminded not to abuse their positions and instead carry out their responsibilities with integrity, accountability and fairness.
Deputy Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid said leadership was not a privilege to be used for personal gain but a major trust that must be discharged responsibly.
“Therefore, I urge that every decision made must be based on integrity, accountability and a sense of fairness,” he said at the handover ceremony for the Sarawak acting police commissioner and acting chairman of the Sarawak Contingent Persatuan Keluarga Polis (Perkep) at the Sarawak Police Contingent Headquarters here today.
Earlier, he witnessed the handover of duties from PDRM Management Department director Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah, who was also the Sarawak police commissioner, to his deputy DCP Saifullizan Ishak before Mohamad Zainal begins his duties at Bukit Aman.
Abdul Aziz also reminded leaders not to oppress or mistreat their subordinate officers and personnel, but to guide, listen to and protect those under their charge.
He said leadership based on such values was important in creating a fair, harmonious and respectful working environment. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s marine police nab 2,707, record 7,627 cases in national waters this year
Article:
PORT KLANG, Oct 1 — The Marine Police Force (PPM) arrested 2,707 individuals in 7,627 criminal cases in the country’s waters during the first nine months of this year.
Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA) director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said that the success was the result of continuous enforcement through various operations such as Op Taring Gelora, Op Taring Landai, and inter or intra-agency operations.
“From January to September, the team recorded seizures and fines worth RM525 million with the arrest of 2,707 people for various offences.
“The highest offences among them involve the Fisheries Act 1985 with 3,214 cases, the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 (428), the Control of Supplies Control Act 1961 (295), the Immigration Act 1959/63 and the ATIPSOM Act 2007 (213), as well as the Customs Act 1967 (189 cases),” he said at a press conference after officiating the 79th Anniversary celebration of the PPM at the Region One PPM Operations headquarters, Pulau Indah here today.
Mohd Yusri said that the success was also the result of effective bilateral cooperation and patrol coordination with regional enforcement agencies such as Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and the Philippines.
Commenting on the issue of illegal immigrant smuggling, he said that irresponsible parties use various modus operandi to infiltrate the country.
“They are targeting international waters by transferring illegal immigrants to another boat before making a ‘drop point’ to Malaysia, with the focus areas including waters around Perak, Selangor Johor, and the northern part of the Peninsula,” he said.
Meanwhile, Mohd Yusri said that PPM as a whole now has 22 projects under the Malaysia Plan (11MP to 13MP) worth RM1.064 billion.
“For future strategic planning, it involves the application of 19 proposed projects worth RM2.28 billion, including the construction of several operational bases for the team.
“PPM will also receive two aircraft carriers and five Fast Patrol Crafts, each worth RM100 million, to further strengthen the unit’s capability in ensuring the safety of the country’s waters,” he said.
Earlier at the event, Mohd Yusri presented the PPM 2026 Hero Award to Sub Inspector (B) Jakarta Makling, 72, in recognition of his contributions and sacrifices throughout his service in the force.
Jakarta, when met, expressed deep emotion over the award that was introduced for the first time since he joined the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) on May 28, 1972.
“In June 1976, while serving as a patrol boat crew member, I was involved in a battle with a group of armed pirates in the waters of Lahad Datu, Sabah, and was shot in the left shoulder.
“The bullet still remains in my shoulder to this day and serves as a testament to my sacrifice in carrying out my duty to protect the safety of the nation’s waters,” said the grandfather of 13 from Semporna, Sabah. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia plans A-to-D food grades to nudge manufacturers — and consumers — towards healthier choices
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Malaysia could introduce a new food labelling system giving packaged food and drinks nutrition grades from A to D by the end of this year, Health Ministry official Dr Yap Wei Aun has said.
Dr Yap, chief executive officer of the Health Ministry’s Health Transformation Office, said prevention was a fundamental aspect of public health and cited the proposed labelling system as an example of the government’s preventive health initiatives.
He said the labels could help nudge Malaysians towards healthier food choices without relying on individual willpower alone, while also encouraging the food and beverage industry to reformulate products to make them healthier.
“At the population level, I’m a little bit less convinced that we can depend on willpower and education to really drive lifestyle change,” he said yesterday during the “Innovating for Retirement Wellbeing” panel session at the Employees Provident Fund’s (EPF) International Social Wellbeing Conference (ISWC) 2026.
Dr Yap said the Health Ministry had been working with partners, including the food industry, to introduce the “front-of-pack labelling” system, under which bottles of drinks or packaged food would carry an A, B, C or D grade.
An A grade would represent the healthiest option, while D would indicate the least healthy.
“So now does it depend on the person per se? Actually, the main effect of this is behaviour change happening at the industry level, in terms of reformulating these foods so that they meet the A and B criteria, rather than the C and D criteria.
“And then when these foods go out, you don’t even depend on consumer choice, prices, availability. The whole health environment has changed,” he said, adding that the approach would reduce reliance on public education alone.
“So, we were collaborating, there’s a terms of reference and a committee jointly with Singapore, because we realised that we share the same food environment. And hopefully this will be rolled out,” he said.
“So we are aiming for gazettement probably end of the year,” he added.
Dr Yap said the measure was among initiatives being developed to address major health risks including physical inactivity and mental health, as well as dietary risks in Malaysia involving “too much salt, too much sugar, and too much calories overall”.
Although the new labelling system may appear to be primarily a “consumer choice” initiative, he said it could work alongside other public health policies to encourage healthier lifestyles by changing the wider food environment.
“Imagine if you are a school — you can just decide we will only serve A and B in the school compound. If you are doing government procurement, if you are an employer, you are only going to make A and B available,” he said.
He said other measures could include restricting advertising for less healthy products and changing how food is presented in retail spaces.
File photo of Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad, whose ministry is developing a mandatory Nutri-Grade system to classify food and drinks according to their nutritional content. — Picture by Choo Choy May
Nutri-Grade in Malaysia and Singapore
While Dr Yap did not use the term “Nutri-Grade” to describe the front-of-pack labelling system, Singapore currently uses the term, which has also previously been cited by Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad in relation to Malaysia’s plans.
In a written parliamentary reply on October 27, 2025, Dzulkefly said Malaysia already had a voluntary front-of-pack food labelling system known as the Healthier Choice Logo (HCL), which assesses nutritional components including fat, salt and sugar content.
At the time, 1,002 food and beverage products had received HCL recognition.
In the same reply, Dzulkefly said Malaysia was developing a mandatory Nutri-Grade system based on sugar levels in drinks, which would be introduced in stages, beginning with ready-to-drink products before being extended to freshly prepared beverages.
Under the proposed system, Dzulkefly said advertising would be completely banned for drinks given a D grade — those containing more than 10g of sugar per 100ml — on any platform.
He said the measure was intended to encourage manufacturers to reformulate their products and reduce sugar levels.
Dzulkefly said Malaysia’s Nutri-Grade system was initially focusing on the sugar content of drinks because the National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) 2024 showed an increase in sugar intake among Malaysians, with more than half of free-sugar intake coming from beverages.
According to the World Health Organisation, free sugars include those added to food and drinks by manufacturers, cooks or consumers, as well as sugars naturally present in honey, syrups, fruit juices and fruit juice concentrates.
In Singapore, the
Nutri-Grade system
assigns drinks grades from A to D based on their sugar and saturated fat content.
Nutri-Grade labels are mandatory for drinks graded C and D, while advertising for products given a D grade is prohibited.

Title: Three separate drug busts net RM3.44m in drugs, five arrests in Penang
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 1 — Penang police arrested five people, including a couple, and seized various types of drugs worth RM3.44 million in three separate operations between September 21 and 27.
Penang Police Chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the raids by the state Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) resulted in the seizure of 8.83 kilogrammes (kg) of heroin, 15.06 kg of methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) powder, five litres of liquid MDMA, 182 ecstasy pills and 70 grammes (g) of ketamine.
He said in the first operation at 3.30pm on September 21, police arrested a 47-year-old local man by the roadside at Jalan Masjid Negeri, before questioning led them to a car parked nearby which was believed to have been used to store drugs and drug-processing equipment.
“An inspection found 8.83 kg of heroin, 5.35 kg of caffeine powder and heroin-processing equipment, with the total value of the seizure estimated at RM443,518.
“The suspect is believed to have obtained the drug supply from a syndicate before repackaging it for sale to buyers,” he said at a press conference at the Penang Police Contingent Headquarters here today.
The following day at about 8.50pm, police conducted two raids around Jalan Tun Dr Awang and Sungai Nibong Kecil, arresting two local men and a foreign woman, all aged between 27 and 42.
Lim said police seized 3.26 kg of MDMA powder and five litres of liquid MDMA, estimated to be worth RM1.2 million, while investigations found that the couple worked at entertainment centres and obtained the MDMA supply from a drug distribution syndicate.
In the third operation at about 11.30 pm on September 27, police from the Machang Bubuk Police Station arrested a 45-year-old local man at Jalan Seladang, Bukit Mertajam, and seized 11.8 kg of MDMA powder, 182 ecstasy pills, heroin and 70 g of ketamine from his car, with the total seizure estimated at RM1.8 million.
According to Lim, intelligence found that the five suspects were believed to have been active in drug trafficking activities in Penang since July, while the three syndicates were not linked to one another.
He said preliminary urine screening found all five suspects were negative for drugs, while checks showed that one of them, namely the first suspect, had previous criminal and narcotics records.
“Following the three raids, police also seized six vehicles of various types worth RM58,000 under the Dangerous Drugs (Forfeiture of Property) Act 1988.
“All suspects have been remanded for seven days to assist investigations, with the cases investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952,” he said. — Bernama

Title: F1 fever builds as PM Anwar takes pit-lane walk at Sepang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Formula 1 fever moved up a gear at the Sepang International Circuit today as Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim joined a Pit Lane Walk on the eve of the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
Video and photographs from the event showed Anwar making his way through the busy pit lane as teams carried out final preparations, with mechanics, equipment and activity around the garages offering a close-up glimpse of the race weekend to come.
He was accompanied by Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
The Pit Lane Walk gave guests a rare look inside the paddock and garage areas before track action begins from October 2 to 4.
This weekend’s race marks Formula 1’s return to Sepang after a nine-year absence, with the circuit last hosting a world championship round in 2017.
Interest has been strong, with nearly 100,000 tickets sold as of Wednesday — a record for races held at the circuit, according to Sepang International Circuit chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif. About 3,000 tickets remained available.
More than 200,000 spectators are expected over the three-day event, prompting Kuala Lumpur International Airport to advise racegoers to use public transport because of limited parking and heavier traffic in the area.
The circuit has also undergone final track works ahead of Formula 1’s return, including surface levelling to remove irregularities in the asphalt and cleaning operations to improve conditions.
Malaysia is staging the event under the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix banner following an agreement involving Formula 1, the FIA and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.

Title: Finance Ministry: Monthly SARA aid credited to recipients’ MyKad from today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Monthly Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) aid has begun being credited to recipients through their respective MyKad cards from today.
The Finance Ministry (MoF), in a post on X today, said RM100 in monthly SARA aid would be credited to households receiving Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR), while senior citizens and single individuals would each receive RM50 a month.
For recipients of both STR and eKasih, households will receive RM200 in monthly SARA aid, while senior citizens will receive RM150 and single individuals RM100.
MoF said 15 categories of goods have been approved for purchase using SARA, covering more than 140,000 essential items such as rice, eggs, bread, cooking oil, over-the-counter medicines, frozen food, canned food and school supplies.
SARA can be used at more than 14,700 selected supermarkets and grocery stores nationwide.

Title: Weather alert: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast across KL, Putrajaya, Labuan and 10 states until 7pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Labuan and 10 states until 7pm today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the adverse weather was expected to affect several areas in Kedah, namely Kuala Muda, Sik and Baling; Perak, including Hulu Perak, Selama, Kerian, Larut Matang, Kuala Kangsar, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk; and Kelantan, covering Kuala Krai and Jeli.
The same warning was issued for Kemaman, Dungun and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu; Rompin, Maran, Temerloh and Bera in Pahang; and Hulu Langat, Hulu Selangor, Kuala Selangor, Klang, Gombak, Petaling, Sepang and Kuala Langat in Selangor, reported Bernama.
In Negeri Sembilan, the affected areas are Seremban and Port Dickson, while in Johor they are Segamat, Tangkak, Muar, Kluang, Batu Pahat, Johor Bahru, Kulai and Pontian.
In Sarawak, the warning covers Mukah (Matu, Dalat, Mukah and Daro), Sibu (Selangau and Sibu), Kapit (Kapit, Bukit Mabong and Song), Bintulu, Miri (Subis), Limbang, Sri Aman (Sri Aman, Pantu and Lingga), Samarahan, Betong, Serian and Kuching.
In Sabah, the affected areas are the Interior (Beaufort, Membakut, Sipitang, Tambunan, Keningau, Tenom and Kuala Penyu) and the West Coast (Papar, Penampang, Tuaran, Kota Kinabalu, Putatan and Kota Belud).

Title: Health Ministry warns against GB Daily Glow Skin Cream after mercury found
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has cancelled the notification of the cosmetic product GB Daily Glow Skin Cream after it was found to contain scheduled poisons, mercury, and is no longer allowed to be sold in the country.
It said that mercury is banned in cosmetics because it can be absorbed into the body and cause damage to the kidneys and nervous system.
“It (mercury) can also disrupt the brain development of young children or unborn babies.
“It can also cause rashes, irritation, and other changes to the skin,” according to the MOH in a statement today.
Following that, the ministry urged the public to avoid buying and using the involved cosmetics.
Members of the public who are using this cosmetic are advised to stop using it immediately and seek advice from a healthcare professional if they experience any discomfort or adverse effects.
“The public is encouraged to check the notification status of a cosmetic product and the list of cancelled cosmetics by visiting the official National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA) website www.npra.gov.my,” according to the statement.
The statement said that the involved sellers and distributors of the cosmetics must immediately cease the sale and distribution of the cosmetics.
“The sale and distribution of this cosmetic are in violation of the Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984,” added the statement.
Individuals who commit an offence under the relevant regulations may be subjected to a maximum fine of RM25,000 or imprisonment not exceeding three years or both for the first offence, and a maximum fine of RM50,000 or imprisonment not exceeding five years or both for subsequent offences.
Companies that commit offences can be fined up to RM50,000 for the first offence and up to RM100,000 for subsequent offences. — Bernama

Title: Indonesia remains a favourite destination for Malaysians as August arrivals jump nearly 29pc
Article:
JAKARTA, Oct 1 — Malaysians remained Indonesia’s largest source of foreign tourists in August, with arrivals jumping 28.95 per cent year-on-year to 296,227.
According to Statistics Indonesia (BPS), Malaysian visitors accounted for 18.52 per cent of the 1.60 million foreign tourist arrivals recorded during the month.
“Foreign tourists visiting Indonesia in August 2026 were dominated by Malaysian passport holders at 18.52 per cent, followed by Australia at 10.75 per cent and China at 10.16 per cent,” it said in its latest tourism statistics released on Thursday.
BPS said overall foreign tourist arrivals in August rose 6.27 per cent from a year earlier, while arrivals from January to August reached 10.58 million, up 5.38 per cent from the corresponding period in 2025.
Meanwhile, it said Malaysia was also the leading overseas destination for Indonesian travellers in August, accounting for 32.64 per cent of outbound trips, followed by Saudi Arabia at 18.58 per cent and Singapore at 14.00 per cent. — Bernama

Title: Kuala Terengganu High Court awards RM47,000 to boy who broke leg after being ‘slammed’ onto chair by teacher
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The Kuala Terengganu High Court today awarded RM47,000 in damages and costs to a boy, now 13, who suffered a broken right leg in an incident involving a Quran and Fardu Ain (KAFA) teacher four years ago.
Judge Yusrin Faidz Yusoff allowed Muhammad Izz Anaqi Mohd Izwan’s appeal and set aside an earlier Sessions Court decision that had dismissed his claim,
Utusan Malaysia
reported.
The judge found that the lower court had erred by failing to properly assess the testimony of two eyewitnesses and a specialist medical report from Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital.
“The judge failed to assess the evidence of two eyewitnesses and the specialist medical report from Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital. The medical report confirmed that the pupil’s [the plaintiff’s] leg injury was caused by a forceful impact,” Yusrin Faidz said in delivering his judgment.
The High Court ordered KAFA teacher Ahmad Mursyidin Abdullah, 41, and his employer, Yayasan Islam Terengganu (YIT), to pay RM30,000 in general damages for the boy’s injuries and RM17,000 in costs, together with interest.
Yusrin Faidz also ruled that YIT was vicariously liable for the injuries suffered by the boy as a result of the teacher’s actions.
According to the statement of claim filed through Muhammad Izz Anaqi’s mother, Nor Azlina Mohamad Yasin, 41, Ahmad Mursyidin allegedly slammed the boy onto a chair at about 3.30pm on July 6, 2022.
The boy was unable to walk home after the class and was taken to a private clinic, where an X-ray confirmed that his right leg was fractured.
Muhammad Izz Anaqi, who is now a student at a Mara Junior Science College (MRSM), was represented by lawyers Mohammad Rafaei Adnan, Mohd Hazwan Hamidun and Alif Danial Ahmad Shahrulnizam.
Saifuddin Othman and Yuhana Junaidi represented the two defendants.

Title: Anwar thanks outgoing China ambassador for strengthening ties with Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today expressed his appreciation to outgoing Chinese Ambassador to Malaysia, Ouyang Yujing, for his commitment and contribution towards strengthening cooperation between the two countries.
Anwar conveyed his appreciation when he received a farewell call from Ouyang today.
He said Malaysia and China had built strong ties across various sectors, including the economy, technology, education and culture.
Strategic cooperation in areas such as the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL), 5G technology, artificial intelligence, ports and the rare earths industry had also opened up new opportunities for mutual benefit, he said.
“Both countries will continue to strengthen the longstanding friendship and cooperation between us, while exploring new areas for the benefit of our people and the peace and prosperity of the region,” Anwar said in a Facebook post.
During the meeting, Anwar said he also received a special gift from Chinese Premier Li Qiang —  a book about Hangzhou, which he recently visited and which is Li’s hometown.
“I deeply appreciate the thought and gesture,” he said.
Anwar undertook a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou from September 22 at Li’s invitation.
The visit focused on two main engagements — the WorldSkills competition in Shanghai and the Global Digital Trade Expo in Hangzhou. — Bernama

Title: Selangor employers who chose Sultan’s Silver Jubilee Oct 25 holiday must observe it, says Labour Dept
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 1 — The special public holiday on October 25 in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee of the 25-year reign of the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, must be observed by private-sector employers in Selangor who have chosen it as one of their paid public holidays.
The Department of Labour Peninsular Malaysia (JTKSM) said employers who designate Sunday as a rest day must provide a replacement paid public holiday on October 26 (Monday), in accordance with Section 60D(1) of the Employment Act 1955.
“Alternatively, with the agreement of their employees, employers may replace the paid public holiday with another day, in accordance with the Act,” it said in a statement today.
The department said the special public holiday was declared under subsection 9(1) of the Holidays Act 1951 [Act 369], which allows the state government to declare any day as a public holiday in the state.
On September 11, the Selangor state government announced October 26 as a replacement public holiday for the entire state following the declaration of October 25 as a special public holiday in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee celebration.
Selangor State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin said the replacement holiday was declared because the celebration and the special public holiday fell on a Sunday. — Bernama

Title: Nga Kor Ming offers one month’s ministerial salary for top Housing Ministry innovator
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming has called for every innovation developed by ministry personnel to translate into tangible benefits for the people by saving time and costs, optimising resources, and improving the speed and effectiveness of service delivery.
He said there is ample scope for innovation at the Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) as it oversees housing, local government, cleanliness and solid waste management, fire and rescue services, as well as urban planning, all of which have a direct impact on people’s lives.
“I hope efforts to foster a culture of innovation among KPKT personnel will continue to be strengthened and expanded, ensuring that innovation goes beyond competitions and becomes a consistent part of public service delivery,” he said.
He said this in his speech at the 2026 Ministry of Housing and Local Government Innovation Day (HIKPKT 2026) here today.
Nga said the ministry should expand, replicate and scale up proven innovations so they can deliver benefits on a larger scale.
Nga also pledged a reward equivalent to one month of a minister’s salary for KPKT personnel who win the Prime Minister’s Innovation Award, to further strengthen the ministry’s culture of innovation.
HIKPKT 2026, themed “
Memperkasa Inovasi, Memacu Prestasi, Menyejahtera Rakyat
”, showcased 54 innovation projects, including 43 Innovative and Creative Group (KIK) projects and 11 Minister’s Innovation Award (AIM) projects.
The Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) took the top two places in the AIM competition, with its BM Fighter team winning with the Checkpoint Tracker project and Sungai Bakap Strategic team finishing runner-up.
Penang JBPM director Mohamad Shoki Hamzah said Checkpoint Tracker was developed to help rescue teams locate people who get lost in forests, shortening search times and reducing operational costs and the number of personnel required.
“If someone gets lost in the forest, we can determine where they are. The team can then go directly to their location and bring them out of the area,” he said.
He said the system uses Global Positioning System (GPS) technology, an SOS emergency feature and a Progressive Web App (PWA), with hikers required to scan a quick response (QR) code before entering forested areas to enable their location and movements to be monitored.
Meanwhile, Puchong Fire and Rescue Station chief Muhammad Azizul Hakim Idris said his team’s Rescue Flex innovation combines three functions to address neck, arm and leg injuries, earning first place in the Department and Agency KIK category.
He said the innovation saves time and eases the burden on rescue personnel by reducing the need to carry multiple pieces of equipment during emergency operations, including accident response and search-and-rescue missions.
“The biggest challenge was developing a concrete idea capable of delivering a significant impact. With the support of the whole team, we were able to turn Rescue Flex into a low-cost, high-impact innovation,” he said. — Bernama
